threats.reasoning:
Brute force compromise detected from IP 198.51.100.99: 5 failed logins within 300s followed by successful login as user 'root'.

🛡️ Actionable Solutions & Remediation Playbook:
[IMMEDIATE CONTAINMENT] Block attacker IP 198.51.100.99 at network and host firewall:
  • Linux iptables: sudo iptables -A INPUT -s 198.51.100.99 -j DROP
  • Linux ufw: sudo ufw deny from 198.51.100.99
  • Windows Firewall: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="Block-198.51.100.99" dir=in action=block remoteip=198.51.100.99
[ACCOUNT REMEDIATION] Terminate active sessions and force password reset for user 'root':
  • Linux session kill: sudo pkill -u root -9
  • Linux password reset: sudo passwd -l root (lock) or sudo passwd root (reset)
  • Windows lock: Disable-LocalUser -Name 'root' or Set-ADUser 'root' -Enabled $false
[SYSTEM HARDENING] Long-term protection against credential attacks:
  • Disable SSH password authentication: set 'PasswordAuthentication no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config
  • Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA / Duo / Google Authenticator) for all remote logins
  • Install and configure automated IP banning: sudo apt install fail2ban

threats.reasoning:
Suspicious command execution detected: Interactive bash reverse shell redirection via /dev/tcp. Matched pattern: 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/10'. Host: host01, User: 'attacker'.

🛡️ Actionable Solutions & Remediation Playbook:
[CRITICAL CONTAINMENT] Immediately isolate host 'host01' from the network:
  • Linux disable network: sudo ip link set dev eth0 down
  • Windows disable network: Disable-NetAdapter -Name 'Ethernet*' -Confirm:$false
[PROCESS TERMINATION] Identify and kill rogue command and reverse shell processes:
  • Linux: ps aux | grep -E 'nc|bash|sh|python|socat' | grep -v grep
  • Kill rogue PID: sudo kill -9 <PID>
  • Windows: Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.CommandLine -match 'powershell|cmd|certutil'}
[PERSISTENCE AUDITING] Inspect scheduled tasks and startup locations for backdoors:
  • Linux crontabs: sudo crontab -l; sudo ls -la /etc/cron.* /var/spool/cron/crontabs
  • Linux systemd services: sudo systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled
  • Check writable staging dirs: sudo ls -lat /tmp /dev/shm /var/tmp
  • Windows persistence: Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object {$_.State -ne 'Disabled'}
[CREDENTIAL REVOCATION] Rotate all service account tokens and SSH authorized_keys present on this host.

threats.reasoning:
SQL Injection payload pattern detected in HTTP request from 198.51.100.88: '/search.php?id=1 UNION SELECT username,password FROM users'.

🛡️ Actionable Solutions & Remediation Playbook:
[PERIMETER MITIGATION] Block source IP 198.51.100.88 on your Web Application Firewall (WAF) or Reverse Proxy:
  • Nginx block: add 'deny 198.51.100.88;' to /etc/nginx/conf.d/blocklist.conf and run 'nginx -s reload'
  • Apache block: Require not ip 198.51.100.88
  • Cloudflare WAF: Add IP Access Rule to block 198.51.100.88
[CODE-LEVEL REMEDIATION] Patch vulnerable web application endpoints:
  • SQL Injection: Replace raw SQL string concatenation with Parameterized Queries (Prepared Statements)
  • XSS: Enforce Context-Aware Output HTML Encoding and configure Content-Security-Policy (CSP) headers
  • Path Traversal: Canonicalize filenames with os.path.realpath() and disallow '..' path segments
[DATABASE SECURITY] Enforce principle of least privilege for web application database accounts:
  • Revoke administrative/SUPERUSER rights from web application DB users
  • Disable database command execution functions (e.g. xp_cmdshell in MSSQL)
